newsitem.title: GERMANY: Asiana wins OK for twice-weekly Germany flights.
newsitem.headline: Asiana wins OK for twice-weekly Germany flights.

text.p: Korean carrier Asiana Airlines said it has won final permission to launch flights to Germany with a twice-weekly service.
Asiana will fly Mondays and Thursdays from Frankfurt to Seoul from May 29 with a Boeing 747 Combi aircraft with 35 tonnes of airfreight capacity.
The airline's newly-appointed Germany cargo traffic supervisor Sasa Kantar told Reuters: "We will definitely have two flights. We wanted to start with two flights and permission has now been given."
Industry sources added that Asiana had reached agreement with Deutsche Lufthansa AG over the second weekly flight.
Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), owner and operator of Frankfurt airport, said in March that Asiana would operate a twice-weekly service but announced in mid-April it would only be a weekly flight.

Kantar, formerly with Korean Airlines, added that German airfreight would be trucked to Amsterdam for the new Asiana weekly B747-400 freighter service starting May 17. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
